title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: a late declaration fee owed must be on the account before a review is decided
content:
## Rule
A late declaration fee owed on the acceptance's signed initial declaration is on its account before its review is decided.

Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product this is so because such a fee can be booked only while the acceptance is still undecided. The fee is owed when the signed initial declaration's lead time — the calendar days from its signing date, which is the date its signed submission was registered, to the scheduled departure (ETD) of the booking carrying the goods — is fewer than the category's declaration lead time. Where more than one initial declaration is signed, the latest of them is the one considered. The fee is settled once a late-declaration-fee row referencing that signed initial declaration is on the acceptance's account. A declaration with a sufficient lead time, or an acceptance whose booking shows no scheduled departure, owes no such fee.

## Truth table
| Lead time compared with the category's figure | Late-fee row referencing the signed initial declaration | Condition for deciding the review |
|---|---|---|
| at least the figure | not needed | met — no fee is owed |
| fewer | on the account | met |
| fewer | not on the account | not met — the review is not decided |
| booking shows no ETD | not needed | met — no fee is owed |

## Worked case (hypothetical lead-time figure of 6 calendar days)
The signed initial declaration was registered on 1 July; the booking's ETD is 5 July. The lead time is 4 days, fewer than 6, so a late declaration fee is owed. With no late-fee row referencing that declaration on the account, the review is not decided; with such a row on the account, this condition is met.

## Points of judgement
- *A late-fee row on the account references an earlier declaration, not the signed initial declaration considered — is the condition met?* No; the row must reference that signed initial declaration.
